dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For x indexed by Fin n, this is sqrt(sum over j in Fin n of x(j)^2) divided by sqrt(n), where n is cast to a real number.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines every left-hand side in the local hypotheses and the conclusion: an RMS-like Euclidean magnitude with exact formula sqrt(sum of squares)/sqrt(n).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For term indexed by Fin m and Fin n, it is the vector whose j-th coordinate is the sum over all i in Fin m of term(i,j).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The decomposition hypothesis requires total to equal the coordinatewise sum of all term vectors.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For x indexed by Fin n, it is the real square root of LocalDef004(x), hence the square root of the sum of the coordinate squares.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the numerator of LocalDef001.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For x indexed by Fin n, it is the finite sum over all i in Fin n of x(i)^2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the measured quantity depend on the exact sum of squared coordinates.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Polymorphic propositional equality between two objects of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses the exact equality between total and the coordinatewise sum defined by LocalDef002.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite type of natural-number indices strictly less than n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fin m indexes the terms, K values, and remainders, while Fin n indexes vector coordinates.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: It equips Fin n with a finite enumeration containing every index exactly once.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms coordinatewise term sums, sums of squares, the sum of all K(i), and the sum of all remainder(i).

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ

binders: For arbitrary natural numbers m and n.
For an arbitrary family term assigning a real vector term(i,·) of length n to each i in Fin m.
For an arbitrary real vector total of length n.
For arbitrary real numbers epsilon and yRms.
For arbitrary real-valued functions K and remainder on Fin m.
hypotheses: For every coordinate j in Fin n, total(j) equals the sum over i in Fin m of term(i,j).
For every i in Fin m, RMS_n(term(i,·)) is at most epsilon*K(i)*yRms + remainder(i).
conclusions: RMS_n(total) is at most epsilon*(sum over i in Fin m of K(i))*yRms + sum over i in Fin m of remainder(i).
mathematical_definitions: RMS_n(x) := sqrt(sum over j in Fin n of x(j)^2) / sqrt(n), with n embedded in the real numbers and Lean's totalized real division.
total = sum over i in Fin m of term(i,·) means exact coordinatewise equality: total(j) = sum over i in Fin m of term(i,j) for every j.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite family of real vectors term(i,·), if total is exactly their coordinatewise sum and each term's quantity sqrt(sum of coordinate squares)/sqrt(n) is bounded above by epsilon*K(i)*yRms plus remainder(i), then the same quantity for total is bounded above by epsilon times the sum of all K(i), times yRms, plus the sum of all remainder(i).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimensions m and n are unrestricted natural numbers and may be zero.
When n is zero, both relevant finite coordinate sums and sqrt(n) are zero; Lean's totalized real division makes LocalDef001 equal to zero rather than mathematically undefined.
When m is zero, the local hypothesis is vacuous, the decomposition forces total to be the zero vector, and both sums on the concluding right-hand side are zero.
No nonnegativity assumptions are imposed on epsilon, yRms, K(i), or remainder(i).
Because LocalDef001 is nonnegative, a negative local right-hand side makes the corresponding local hypothesis impossible, so the implication has no admissible hypotheses in that case.
The symbol yRms is only an arbitrary real parameter; the proposition does not define it as, or relate it to, the RMS-like quantity of any vector.
The decomposition is exact, with no decomposition error or approximation term.
The measured quantity is specifically sqrt(sum of squares)/sqrt(n), not a general norm and not a coordinatewise or maximum norm.
No componentwise bounds, absolute-error interpretation, probabilistic assumptions, or sign conditions are encoded.
